staged_original_note: The twice-rebuilt file, UNCHANGED at Book XI step 1. It was rebuilt at Book IV step 1 (three PG illustration captions; 7bf2d1b1... -> b0ecf3da...) and at Book VII step 1 (three of Long's footnotes printed flush left; b0ecf3da... -> 7798607d...). For Book XI the check was NOT a re-run of the build script, and the reconstruction's own RULES were audited against the raw range before its output was looked at -- the Book IX reviewer established that byte-identity to a re-run proves only that the file matches the script, and the Book X reviewer established that a reconstruction sharing a blind spot with the build proves nothing either. scripts/verify_book11_source.py, written from scratch, reports the rule audit and then diffs PG lines 6376-6816 (after the XI. header at 6375, before the XII. header at 6817) word for word against the staged Book XI. It reconstructs 39 paragraphs, matching the staged count, and THE ONLY DIFFERENCES IN THE WHOLE BOOK ARE THE THREE DAGGER MARKS at XI.8 (PG 6488), XI.15 (PG 6544) and XI.17 (PG 6577), which PROVENANCE.md section 4 documents as deliberately removed. Rule audit, class by class: SEVENTEEN maximal indented runs enumerated with their indentation profiles -- eleven footnote runs, all indented four spaces (openers at PG 6398, 6401, 6420, 6459, 6461, 6554, 6647, 6702, 6750, 6753, 6757), consumed in seven blocks because notes separated only by a blank line are consumed together; three verse runs in XI.6 (PG 6441-6442, 6446, 6450) indented SIX spaces, with flush-left text standing between every verse run and every footnote run, so no verse can have been swallowed; two verse citations (PG 6777 indented 26, PG 6780 indented 17), kept in the staged original under D5 and dropped from the candidate; and one unmarked continuation of footnote [A]'s two-paragraph body (PG 6558-6559), consumed with the note it belongs to. ELEVEN in-text markers -- ten in flush-left text plus one at the end of the indented verse line 6442 -- reconciling exactly with the eleven openers. NO flush-left footnote opener (the VII.45 class) and no flush-left footnote body, which would have shown as a diff. NO illustration caption (the Book IV class). Only three standalone short flush-left lines, all Long's own connectives in XI.6. No Greek in the body (all five [Greek: ...] spans are inside indented footnote bodies). ONE RULE OF THE BUILD WAS FOUND UNDOCUMENTED and is now documented in PROVENANCE.md section 4: a space before , ; : . ? ! is closed up, which produced a fourth diff at XI.18 on the first run; it fires in exactly five lines in the whole translation body (IV.19, V.29, VII.58, VII.66, XI.18), all at ellipses marking lacunae, and changes no word, so NO REBUILD was made and D12's standard is not engaged. sha256 still 7798607d..., 487 paragraphs, 12 chapters, section profile 17,17,16,51,36,59,75,61,42,38,39,36, git status clean. No accepted book is reopened.

word_counts.note: screening signal only; not evidence of semantic completeness. 0.977 is the lowest book ratio in the package, and THE WHOLE OF THE SHORTFALL IS APPARATUS: eleven cross-reference spans, six source citations (two verse citations and four Epictetus references) and five brackets dropped under D11, 89 words in all. The three lowest paragraphs are three of the shortest meditations in the book, whose entire difference is a dropped citation -- XI.32 (0.64, a five-word Hesiod citation of fourteen words), XI.31 (0.67, a three-word Odyssey citation of nine) and XI.36 (0.71, a four-word Epictetus reference of fourteen) -- then XI.33 (0.87), XI.12 (0.91) and XI.35 (0.92), again dropped citations and cross-references. Of the paragraphs carrying no apparatus at all, NONE is below 0.96 (XI.7), and twenty-two of the thirty-nine sit between 0.99 and 1.02. Maximum 1.02 at XI.3, where one 'to' is supplied. SEVEN paragraphs are byte-identical to Long (XI.14, XI.22, XI.24, XI.25, XI.28, XI.38, XI.39), more than in any earlier book.

dagger_marks: Three in Book XI of the PG text, in three sections: XI.8 (line 6488), XI.15 (line 6544), XI.17 (line 6577). Each named in review-instructions.md with its PG line number and kept as Long has it, with pronouns modernised and glossary renderings applied (the VI.50 reading, confirmed at VII.16, enforced at VIII.51, applied at IX.6/26/27 and X.9/19/25/31). Matches PROVENANCE.md section 4. XI.8's falls between 'tree,' and 'but'. XI.15's and XI.17's each fall immediately after one of Long's commas, and BOTH COMMAS ARE KEPT on the X.25 ruling, which the Book X round-1 reviewer confirmed: a comma closing a long relative subject is a rhythm mark, not a syntax error, and removing it would be a stylistic change inside a dagger clause.

shall_rule: Third book drafted under the rule fixed at Book VIII acceptance and widened at Book IX acceptance. Long has 8 shall/shalt in Book XI; the candidate keeps 2 and removes 6, every one of the six a plain future. The two kept are both in XI.18 and both licensed twice over: 'How then shall I take away these opinions?' (first person AND the deliberative shall of a direct question, the VIII.1 case) and 'I shall certainly not be injured' (first person, the II.1 / VIII.45 case). Removed: XI.13 'Suppose any man shall despise me' -> 'despises' (a supposition, a clause of condition); XI.13 'Shall any man hate me?' -> 'Will any man hate me?' (a direct third-person question, but a RHETORICAL future and not a deliberative one, so the widened Book IX clause does not reach it -- the X.11 / X.32 ruling in its third book); XI.19 'when thou shalt reproach thyself' -> 'when you reproach yourself' (time); XI.20 'until again the universal shall sound' -> 'until the whole again sounds' (time); XI.21 'an object which shall be' -> 'which is' (the positive consecutive shape ruled on at X.1); XI.29 'before thou shalt have first learned' -> 'before you have first learned' (time, present perfect). No second-person and no plain-future shall survives. Book XI adds no new case to the three third-person plain futures already standing in accepted books (III.9, VII.8, VII.24).
base_text_defects: XI.18 PG 'thou must equally avoid NATTERING men and being vexed at them' (line 6797); Standard Ebooks reads 'flattering', Long writes 'flatter' of exactly this at XI.14, and the sentence pairs flattery against resentment. Rendered 'flattering'. FLAGGED - the one departure from PG's letters in Book XI.

XI.18, in the SAME clause, PG is right and SE is wrong: PG 'being VEXED at them', SE 'being VEIED at them', which is not a word. Each text carries a slip in the same eleven words and each gets right what the other gets wrong. PG followed, and 'vexed' takes the glossary's 'resenting'.
XI.8 PG 'and again to BECOME a part which helps to make up the whole'; SE 'and BE TO COME a part', garbled. PG followed.
XI.10 PG 'the arts imitate the NATURES of things'; SE 'the NATURE of things'. Long's own next clause is 'the most comprehensive of all natures'. PG followed.
XI.6 PG 'which gradually SANK down'; SE 'SUNK down'. PG is right on grammar and is followed.
XI.10 a PG typographic slip: no full stop after 'the skill of art' before 'Now all arts'; SE has it. Supplied. No word changes.
XI.15 PG 'What ARE thou doing, man?' for 'art'; SE has 'art'. Both become 'What are you doing' under the thou-rule, so the slip does not reach the candidate. The X.32 case.
XI.1 an open variant: PG 'Thus THE right reason differs not at all from the reason of justice'; SE 'Thus THEN right reason differs...'. Both English, both sensible. PG followed under D6.
XI.35 an open variant: PG 'are all changes'; SE 'all are changes'. PG followed under D6.

XI.18 and XI.33 typographic: PG 'wrong-doers' and 'mad-man's'; SE 'wrongdoers' and "madman's". Normalised with SE under the X.36.2 ruling on 'some one' -> 'someone'. Likewise XI.34 'To-morrow' -> 'Tomorrow'.

XI.18, Long's own broken text: 'but either when he is alone, and if others are present...'. His footnote says 'It appears that there is a defect in the text here'; the footnote is apparatus and is not imported, and the ellipsis stands on the V.29 and VII.58 precedent.

Standard Ebooks prints Book XI in more typographic paragraphs than PG, breaking out XI.6's three verse quotations. None is a section break; 39 is the standard section count and extra paragraphs would break the 487-paragraph alignment. The IX.28 and X ruling.
flagged_for_reviewer: XI.18 'flattering' rendered for PG's 'nattering' - the one place in Book XI where the candidate departs from PG's letters; same class as VIII.37 'Pergamus', IX.34 'poor souls' and X.15 'Let men see', all three upheld at round 1.

XI.18's nine-word bracket '[If any have offended against thee, consider first]' FOLDED. The largest bracket in the package. Folded because it is a supplement supplying the occasion of the nine rules and not a remark about the translation, so neither D11 nor the new D13 reaches it, and without it XI.18 opens on 'What is my relation to men' with no frame. The case against it is its size. A ruling is wanted, including on whether D13 should be read to cover a bracket this large.

XI.10 '[things indifferent]' DROPPED under D11. In shape it is exactly X.2's '[social]' and X.15's '[political community]', both settled as drops at Book X round 1. But unlike 'political' and 'law', the primary word Long leaves standing ('middle things') is the LESS transparent of the two. Alternatives: fold it (against the Book X ruling), extend the glossary's 'indifferent' row to cover 'middle things' (which renders the primary word AS the bracket's words and is indistinguishable in the result from folding), or leave it as drafted.

XI.26's '[Ephesians]' FOLDED as a mark of textual doubt. Long brackets the name because the manuscript reading is uncertain -- his footnote reports Gataker's conjecture -- not because the word is a supplement or a second rendering. The candidate removes the brackets and keeps the word, as a dagger's mark is removed and the clause stands. Confirm, or rule that it belongs with the D11 drops or under D13.

XI.15 'at once' for Long's 'forthwith'. X.30 rendered 'forthwith' as 'immediately', but here Long's own 'immediately' stands nine words earlier INSIDE the dagger clause, so the X.30 rendering would invent an echo Long does not have. The clause sits in the dagger SENTENCE though outside the dagger CLAUSE. Confirm, or rule for 'immediately' in both places, or for leaving 'forthwith' alone.
offered_for_confirmation: 'Pancratium' kept untranslated at XI.2, on the X.9 'Mimi' ruling: Long's text and not apparatus, met in a list of three entertainments where the reader takes it for one, and where any gloss would import his footnote.
